response: Inspection reports take too long to be published. By the time families read them, things have often changed in the nursing home.
Please publish inspection findings faster and in plain language. Most families cannot follow the current reports.
Home support needs regulating urgently. My mother has had six different carers in two months and nobody checks the quality.
Regulate home care providers the same way as nursing homes. At the moment there is no independent oversight at all.
Staffing shortages are the real issue. Inspections note the gaps but nothing changes because services cannot recruit.
As a manager of a disability service, the paperwork for inspection takes staff away from residents. Less duplication would help.
Use data better. Providers already submit lots of information; it should be used to spot risks before inspectors visit.
I am Deaf and use Irish Sign Language. Consultations and reports are never available in ISL, so my community is left out.
Children in care should be asked directly about their experience. Surveys mostly reach parents and staff.
More unannounced inspections, especially at night and at weekends when staffing is thinnest.
The National Care Experience surveys are useful. Please extend them to mental health services, which get little attention.
Travellers rarely see themselves in these reports. Engage with Traveller organisations when designing surveys.
Rural services are inspected far less often than city ones. People in rural areas deserve the same assurance.
Reports should show whether things improved after the last inspection, not just list what was wrong.
Measure outcomes for residents, like quality of life and dignity, not just compliance with paperwork.
Faster publication of reports, please. Six months later the information is out of date.
Home support workers are underpaid and overstretched. Regulation without funding will not fix the problem.
Plain English summaries at the top of every report would make a huge difference for families.
There should be a simple way for families to raise concerns between inspections and know what happened next.
Artificial intelligence could help analyse inspection data, but it must be used carefully and transparently.
Mental health services need the same level of independent monitoring as acute hospitals.
Avoid asking providers for the same data in three different formats. Share data between agencies.
